Kuvitus: vasemmalla joen varrella voimal: Illustration: on the left, beside a river, a power plant and its transformer, from which a long power line leaves. Large lattice pylons carry the conductors over fields and forest towards a city seen far away on the right, where lights are on in the windows.
Periaatekuva muuntajasta, ei mittakaavas: Schematic picture of a transformer, not to scale. A primary coil with more turns is wound on the left limb of a closed iron core, and a secondary coil with fewer turns on the right limb. The primary coil is connected to an alternating voltage source whose voltage is U1, and the secondary coil to a lamp whose voltage is U2. A green dashed line with arrows circles inside the iron core: the changing magnetic flux produced by the primary current also passes along the core through the secondary coil.
Kaavakuva sähköverkosta, ei mittakaavass: Schematic picture of the power grid, not to scale. In the top row the generator voltage of the power plant, 20 kV, is raised by a transformer to 400 kilovolts, and the large pylons of the transmission grid carry the electricity to a substation. At the substation a transformer lowers the voltage, and in the bottom row the small pylons of the distribution network carry the 20 kV voltage to a local substation, which lowers it to the 230 volts of homes.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: siirtojohdossa lä: Graph, to scale: the share of the transmitted power that becomes internal energy in a transmission line, as a percentage, as a function of the transmission voltage in kilovolts, when the transmitted power is 200 MW and the resistance of the line 6.0 ohms. The curve falls steeply: at 100 kV the share is 12 %, at 200 kV 3.0 % and at 400 kV 0.75 %. When the voltage doubles, the share falls to a quarter.
Kuvitus: seinäpistorasiaan on kytketty p: Illustration: a small phone charger is plugged into a wall socket, and its cable leads to a phone on a table, which is charging.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: pienoismallin sii: Graph, to scale: the power P_h that becomes internal energy in the transmission line of a model, in watts, as a function of the current I in amperes. Five measurement points at the currents 1.0; 2.0; 3.0; 4.0 and 5.0 A, the powers 0.9; 3.1; 7.4; 12.6 and 20.1 W, and a parabola fitted to the points, which starts from the origin, passes through the grid point (5.0 A; 20 W) and continues as a dashed line after the last measurement point. The grid spacing is 0.5 A and 2 W.
